verdict.rationale: gstack is distributed as a public GitHub repo whose skills are installed onto your own machine, either globally or vendored per project. You can run it straight from your own checkout via dev mode, and it ships its own local headless Chromium daemon, so the core product runs entirely on user-controlled infrastructure. Its AI reasoning still depends on whichever host agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) the user plugs in. Missing for 10: explicit self-hosting or offline-operation documentation, clarity on running without third-party hosted LLM hosts, and independent hands-on corroboration of fully self-contained deployment.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Detects global vs vendored install, runs the upgrade, and shows what's new.
It symlinks your repo into the local `.claude/skills/` directory so Claude Code reads skills straight from your checkout.
gstack falls back, automatically, to the browser it ships itself: a persistent headless Chromium daemon behind a compiled CLI ($B).
Project-local setup never silently replaces a global install.
